exams.title: Computer Networks - Quiz 2
exams.subject: Computer Networks
exams.description: Comprehensive assessment on OSI Reference Model, Transport Layer (TCP/UDP), and IP Routing architectures.
instructions: Negative marking of 0.5 marks applies for incorrect answers.
You can flag questions and review them before submission.
Do not refresh or close the tab while the exam is active.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which topology requires a multipoint connection where all nodes share a single communication line?
questions.explanation: In Bus Topology, all devices are connected along a single backbone cable acting as a multipoint connection.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: What is the primary role of the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP)?
options: Map 32-bit IPv4 address to 48-bit MAC address
Map domain names to IP addresses
questions.explanation: ARP resolves logical network layer IP addresses to physical data link layer MAC addresses.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which class of IPv4 address provides a default subnet mask of 255.255.0.0?
questions.explanation: Class B addresses have a 16-bit network prefix (/16), yielding a default subnet mask of 255.255.0.0.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: What mechanism does TCP utilize to establish a reliable end-to-end full duplex connection?
questions.explanation: TCP sets up connection state via a three-way handshake: SYN from client, SYN-ACK from server, ACK from client.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which layer of the OSI model handles logical addressing and routing?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for packet forwarding, routing, and IP addressing.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which of the following protocols is connectionless and does not guarantee packet delivery order?
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is a lightweight, connectionless protocol without acknowledgments or retransmissions.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: What is the default port number used for secure HTTPS web traffic?
questions.explanation: HTTPS operates over TLS/SSL using standardized TCP port 443.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which protocol is standardly used by email clients to retrieve messages from a mail server while keeping them synchronized across devices?
questions.explanation: IMAP (Internet Message Access Protocol) stores emails on the server and synchronizes changes across all devices.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: What is the purpose of the Congestion Window (cwnd) in TCP?
options: To prevent the receiver buffer from overflowing
To limit the amount of data injected into the network to avoid congestion
To encrypt payload data against man-in-the-middle attacks
To calculate checksum values for transmission errors
questions.explanation: While the receiver advertised window (rwnd) prevents buffer overflow at the receiver, cwnd prevents network congestion.

questions.subject: Computer Networks
questions.text: Which routing protocol uses Dijkstra algorithm to compute the shortest path tree across link states?
questions.explanation: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First) is a link-state routing protocol that utilizes Dijkstra shortest-path-first algorithm.

exams.title: Data Structures - Unit Test 3 — Trees & Graphs
exams.subject: Data Structures
exams.description: Test on Binary Search Trees, Balanced Trees, Graph Traversals, and Heap data structures.
instructions: Passing marks required: 5 out of 10 marks.
Review your answers thoroughly in the question palette before clicking submit.

questions.subject: Data Structures
questions.text: What is the average time complexity of searching an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (BST)?
questions.explanation: In a balanced BST like AVL or Red-Black tree, the height is logarithmic, giving O(log n) search time.

questions.subject: Data Structures
questions.text: Which graph traversal algorithm uses a FIFO Queue data structure?
questions.explanation: BFS explores neighbor nodes level by level using a First-In-First-Out (FIFO) queue.

questions.subject: Data Structures
questions.text: What is the worst-case lookup time in a hash table when severe collisions occur and separate chaining is used without treeification?
questions.explanation: When all keys hash to the same bucket, the linked chain has length n, resulting in O(n) search time.

questions.subject: Data Structures
questions.text: In a Min-Heap with N elements, where is the smallest element always located?
questions.explanation: In any Min-Heap, every parent is smaller than or equal to its children, meaning the minimum element is at the root.

exams.title: Operating Systems - Mid Semester Exam
exams.subject: Operating Systems
exams.description: Midterm examination on CPU Scheduling, Deadlock prevention/avoidance, and Virtual Memory management.
instructions: Calculators and electronic aids are prohibited.
Ensure a stable network connection before starting.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.text: Which scheduling algorithm is non-preemptive and selects the process with the smallest execution burst time?
questions.explanation: Non-preemptive Shortest Job First schedules the process with the shortest CPU burst next and runs it to completion.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.text: Which of the following is NOT one of Coffman four necessary conditions for deadlock?
questions.explanation: The Coffman condition is "No Preemption". If preemption is allowed, deadlock cannot occur.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.text: What phenomenon occurs when a page replacement algorithm causes more page faults as the number of allocated physical frames increases?
questions.explanation: Belady Anomaly can occur in FIFO page replacement where increasing memory frames increases page faults.

exams.title: Database Management Systems - Relational Algebra & SQL
exams.subject: Database Systems
exams.description: Assessment covering Normalization (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) and ACID transaction management.

questions.subject: Database Systems
questions.text: A relation is in Boyce-Codd Normal Form (BCNF) if and only if for every functional dependency X -> Y:
options: X is part of a candidate key
questions.explanation: BCNF requires that every determinant X in non-trivial functional dependencies X -> Y must be a superkey.

questions.subject: Database Systems
questions.text: Which ACID property guarantees that concurrent execution of transactions leaves the database in the same state as if transactions were executed serially?
questions.explanation: Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions execute independently without interfering with each other.
